name: Siefeldin Sobih
intro: Hi, you can call me Saif. I work across biology, data, and code, and enjoy helping people make sense of all three.
bio: My background spans molecular biology, statistical modeling, and science education. I’m drawn to questions that connect living systems with computational tools—and to sharing what I learn along the way.

banner.text: November 2026: I’m updating this website to reflect my new positions and projects.

teaching.heading: Teaching & mentoring
teaching.title: Making biology approachable.
teaching.description: From computational biology to microbiology labs, I enjoy turning difficult concepts into something students can explore and use.

research.heading: Currently working on
research.title: Biology, through a computational lens.
research.description: My research background connects microbiomes, physiology, and conservation. Alongside it, I’m building my skills in machine learning and reproducible analysis.
research.imageAlt: Diagram connecting biological samples, analysis, and interpretation

teaching.description: Teaching assistant. Supporting students as they develop computational approaches to biological questions.
Leading laboratory sessions, preparing presentations, and helping students connect experiments with biological concepts.
Mentoring students, grading assignments, and delivering a guest lecture.

teaching.institution: October University for Modern Sciences & Arts
teaching.description: Teaching laboratory sessions in bioinformatics, advanced genetics, and microbial genetics.

outreach: Through the Biology Graduate Student Association at Utah State University, I’ve helped coordinate science outreach, including Science Unwrapped. Making research accessible to people outside the lab is part of why I teach.
footer: A place for the things I learn, teach, and build.
